title: Japan's main stock index took 34 years to get back to its 1989 high

cover.alt: The stone facade and columned entrance of the Tokyo Stock Exchange building in Kabutocho, Tokyo.

body: On 29 December 1989, at the height of Japan's [asset price bubble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_asset_price_bubble), the **Nikkei 225** touched 38,957.44 and closed at 38,915.87. Then the bubble burst. Over the next two decades the index gave back nearly all of those gains, bottoming at 6,994.90 on 28 October 2008, 82% below the peak. Not until **22 February 2024**, more than 34 years later, did it close above the old record, at 39,098.68; it passed 40,000 on 4 March 2024 and 50,000 in October 2025. The Nikkei is a price-weighted average of 225 large companies listed in Tokyo, calculated since 7 September 1950 and back-dated to May 1949, and run by the Nihon Keizai Shimbun newspaper since 1970.

slides.question: In which year did the Nikkei 225 finally close above its December 1989 record?
slides.explanation: On 22 February 2024 it closed at 39,098.68, above the 1989 close of 38,915.87 at last. The 2008 low of 6,994.90 had been 82% below the peak.

slides.heading: The Nikkei 225 at three moments
slides.note: The index went on to pass 40,000 in March 2024 and 50,000 in October 2025

slides.label: fall from the 1989 peak to the 2008 low
slides.text: Nearly nineteen years after the top, the index stood at 6,994.90 during the global financial crisis.

slides.question: How are the 225 companies weighted in the Nikkei index?
slides.explanation: The Nikkei 225 is a price-weighted index: a company with a high share price moves it more than one with a low share price, whatever their size.
